answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. The mechanism therefore aligns self-interest with network health: an attacker gains most by behaving honestly, because that is the only move that scales. Consider a hollow as the anchor of the cost.
